title: Diagnose the retained prepare-lock refusal during opt-out profile recovery
outcome: Diagnose the retained prepare-lock refusal during opt-out profile recovery
acceptance: Explain and correct the prepare.lock contention that caused task_prepare_pending_profile_drift_guides_without_changing_retained_operation to fail, while preserving immediate refusal for a genuinely held lock and the existing-only opt-out path

Add a deterministic regression for the identified lock lifetime or competing holder; unchanged pending-profile attempts retain their metadata and filesystem state without sleeps, skipped checks or retries until green

completion.summary: Diagnosed and fixed the intermittent 'pending preparation busy' refusal. Task-sync's prepare.lock (progress/resume.rs) and the setup preparation lock (setup/intent.rs) were released only by closing the file. On Unix an flock belongs to the open file description, and a child forked by another thread shares that description until exec, so the lock could stay held with no holder. A new HeldLock (src/task_sync/file_lock.rs) releases by an explicit unlock on drop. Immediate refusal, the error texts and the existing-only opt-out open are unchanged. Two deterministic cfg(unix) regressions use a child holding a duplicated descriptor, with no sleeps or retries. Reviewed in 2 rounds (round 2 clean). Focused runs on DL560: FOCUSED-2 passed all 5 runs, including the originally failing pending-profile test. Landed by Termal::Merger3 with the cache fix as master 3430eadd: pushed, installed build 63d907d1, Windows and DL560 final gates PASS, all stores ready. The post-landing independent evaluation d8e069331716453c9872954a5c4dd7ac passed both criteria.
